text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's collective presidency will reconsider the agreement reached in Sintra, Portugal and call for Belgrade to unconditionally accept establishment of diplomatic ties between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, Bosnia's Ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka says.

- Such (Serb) behaviour is not a serious approach to work of one of the central institutions. Time has come for Serb political games to stop, says deputy to the High Representative to Bosnia, Michael Steiner, after Bosnian Serb delegation failed to show up at a meeting of the country's government.

- A mass grave with more than ten corpses has been found at Sarajevo's western cemetery of Vlakovo. It is believed that the victims were killed at the begining of Bosnian war in 1992 when Vlakovo suburb was under Serb control, newspaper says.
- Sarajevo canton sent 200,000 German Marks donation to the victims of a recent earthquake in Iran, canton president Midhat Haracic says.
- International donors conference for reconstruction of Bosnia will be held but money will go only to those who fulfilled all obligations, says Michael Steiner.
- Turkey renewed its promise to donate $80 million for Bosnia reconstruction, Turkish officials said during a visit of Bosnia's collective presidency chairman Alija Izetbegovic to the country.

- New High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, will have two deputies during his mandate, U.S. Army General Jacques Klein and a German diplomat Gert Wagner, daily quotes a foreign diplomat as saying. -- Sarajevo Newsroom +387-71-663-864.
